signals.title: Replica Barry Sheene leathers help break TWFL record at Silverstone
signals.summary: Two Wheels for Life set a new record total at Silverstone last weekend, after raising €234,000 for supported charities in The Gambia, Nigeria, Lesotho, and Malawi. Two Wheels for Life raised €234,000 (around £200,000) for charity at the British MotoGP last weekend, with €122,000 (roughly £105,000) coming directly from auctions. The funds were raised in support of the charity’s programmes in The Gambia, Nigeria, Lesotho, and Malawi, which provide vital transportation for healthcare services to remote and underprivileged communities. Two Wheels for Life hosted a series of events from Thursday, August 6, to Sunday, August 9, including auctions and the new Silverstone Challenge. The latter saw over 150 fans make donations to ride the MotoGP simulator, with a grid experience for two included as a prize for Sunday’s Grand Prix. The MotoGP grid experience went the way of 16-year-old Kacper Dubanowski, after setting a best time of 1.55:699. This took place on Friday, the same day that saw ten fans participate in a unique pillion ride around the Silverstone circuit aboard Ducati MotoEX2 machines, which were piloted by Ducati test rider, Franco Battaini and former Grand Prix racer Fonsi Nieto. The GP of Champions’ MotoGP Experience Day, which kicked things off on Thursday, proved to be a major success as the event was sold out with 750 guests attending. signals.title: Sylvain Guintoli to auction Sonic the Hedgehog-inspired bike for Luca foundation
signals.summary: Sylvain Guintoli has put his 2000 Bourget custom motorcycle up for auction in a bid to raise funds for the Luca Guintoli charity foundation. Former WorldSBK champion and current TNT Sports MotoGP co-presenter, Sylvain Guintoli, has put his Sega Sonic the Hedgehog-inspired ‘Dark Rider’ motorcycle up for auction, with all proceeds going to the Luca Guintoli charity foundation. The foundation was founded by Sylvain after his late son, Luca, tragically passed away at the age of six last summer, following a near year-long battle with cancer. The motorcycle is a Bourget's Bike Works custom build that is a one-off model designed by Sega in connection with Oil Sweat & Gears and Atmospherics SFX. The ‘Dark Rider’ motorcycle is inspired by Shadow the Hedgehog from Sega's iconic Sonic the Hedgehog franchise, which was known to be a favourite character of Guintoli’s son. In fact, Guintoli recently honoured his son by running the London Marathon in a full one-piece leather suit that featured a specific Sonic the Hedgehog design. By running the marathon alongside his two daughters, Alicia and Layla, Guintoli managed to raise over £150,000 for PASIC (Parents' Association for Seriously Ill Children), which is an organisation that provides help and support to families whose children are fighting cancer. signals.title: Hot weather motorcycle riding tips: 8 ways to stay cool and avoid heat exhaustion
signals.summary: Riding a motorcycle in hot weather can be tough. Here are eight simple ways to stay cool, hydrated and safe when temperatures start to rise. A warm summer's day and an empty road are about as close to motorcycling perfection as it gets. But when temperatures start pushing towards 30°C and beyond, riding a motorcycle can become uncomfortable surprisingly quickly. The problem isn't just that you're hot. Dehydration, fatigue and heat exhaustion can all affect your concentration, reactions and decision-making, which is rather important when you're sitting on a motorcycle surrounded by other road users. That doesn't mean you need to put the bike away whenever the mercury rises. There are plenty of simple things you can do to stay cool while riding a motorcycle in hot weather, without compromising your protective gear or making yourself miserable. If you're heading out for a long ride on a hot day, hydration should be part of your preparation rather than something you think about once you're already thirsty. Riding in the heat, particularly in full motorcycle gear, means you can lose a surprising amount of fluid. You might not notice it while you're concentrating on the road, but the effects of dehydration can creep up on you and leave you feeling tired, sluggish or unable to concentrate properly. signals.title: Track every trip with Cardo’s enhanced Ride Pro app
signals.summary: Cardo is promising a more “connected experience before, during and after every ride”, after announcing further updates to its premium riding app, which now features Android Auto compatibility. Cardo has now bolstered its two-wheeled presence further through a major partnership with Apple, although the company's most recent product update will also please Android users. The partnership sees Cardo’s premium Ride Pro app receive the Apple CarPlay dashboard integration system, meaning more tech, and a more seamless experience will be on offer, according to Cardo. Many modern day motorcycles are equipped with varying TFT screen sizes that support Apple CarPlay, and by entering into this agreement, riders with the Cardo app will be able to access a detailed navigation system, while also managing their journey via a more intuitive interface. In addition to dashboard integration, Cardo’s Ride Pro system includes features such as Tracking, allowing riders to record every trip they go on, as well as viewing their route on an interactive map, and accessing a wide range of riding data. Cardo’s tracking feature also lets riders share their location with friends, which is a useful tool especially for those that ride regularly in larger groups. While the CarPlay technology function will certainly please Apple users, the company's major update is that the app now features Android Auto compatibility, meaning the same features are available across both platforms. signals.title: Sam Sunderland confirms world record attempt this September
signals.summary: Sam Sunderland will attempt to become the fastest person ever to circumnavigate the globe on a motorcycle, with his world record attempt starting in London, on September 5. Two-time Dakar Rally champion Sam Sunderland will take on a world record attempt in September that he was due to try in 2025, before suffering a broken back. Sunderland will attempt to become the fastest rider ever to circumnavigate the globe on a motorcycle, with the time to beat currently standing at 19 days, eight hours, and 25 minutes. Sunderland will begin his world record attempt in London, where he will depart aboard a Triumph Tiger 1200 Rally Explorer, on September 5. The record time that Sunderland will attempt to beat has stood for more than two decades, and represents a huge challenge. To beat the record, Sunderland will need to ride more than 18,000 miles across five different continents, which includes crossing two antipodes and averaging close to 1,000 miles a day. To make sense of these numbers, it is the equivalent of riding the full length of the UK every day. The challenge will be anything but straightforward for Sunderland, though, who will likely be faced with changing climates, while also navigating several border crossings, differing time zones, and fighting against extreme fatigue. Speaking about the challenge that he was originally planning to take on in 2025, Sunderland said: "I've spent months thinking about this challenge while focusing on getting myself fit again. signals.title: Indonesian authorities seize collection of illegal Harley bikes and frames
signals.summary: Authorities in Indonesia have seized a total of five Harley-Davidson motorcycles and 20 frames, with three firms now under investigation. A collection of five Harley-Davidson motorcycles and 20 frames have been seized in Indonesia, with authorities launching an investigation into the potentially illegal shipment from China. According to reports, officials discovered the illegal shipment container during an inspection at Tanjung Priok Port, which is located in North Jakarta. The case has been put under administrative review, although it has not advanced to being a criminal case yet. All five motorcycles have been confirmed as used bikes, while the 20 frames are all for Harley-Davidson models. The reason this could be an illegal shipment is because Indonesia has strict regulations regarding the commercial import of used vehicles. There are limited exceptions to this, however, it is largely prohibited. The law is in place to protect domestic manufacturing and prevent tax avoidance by means of importing used motor vehicles. Three importing companies are currently being investigated over the shipment container, including PAS, which has allegedly imported two of the used motorcycles. TSS is reported to have imported the other three bikes, while it’s claimed that HPM is responsible for the 20 frames. Authorities have so far inspected import documents and carried out interviews with the companies summoned. Customs are also working together with the Tanjung Priok Port police force. Ad

signals.title: Stuck in the mud: Military motorcycle retrieved from the Danube river
signals.summary: A motorcycle used more than 80 years ago in World War II has been found and rescued by a team of experts in the most unlikely of places. A German DKW NZ 350-1 military motorcycle, once used in World War II, has been pulled from underneath rocks and mud in the Danube river, in Budapest. The motorcycle was rescued in surprisingly good condition given the amount of time it had been stuck in the same location. It was also retrieved by a local team of experts, as were human remains and several explosives. Despite being stuck underneath mud for all these years, the bike could still serve as a restoration project as it remains largely intact. As well as the motorcycle mentioned, reports say German and Soviet infantry ammunition, remnants of hand grenades and artillery shells, and German TMi–35 mines were all discovered as well. This means the motorcycle was likely to be one of the safest objects found, however, due to the amount of artillery and explosives, the area was therefore secured before an evacuation could begin. All of these objects were discovered as a result of the Danube’s extremely low water level. Full of mud and trapped water, the bike is said to have weighed over 200 kg, meaning several members of the evacuation team were needed to remove it from where it wallowed. According to Daily News Hungary, the bike was “transported to the hangar of the Military History Institute and Museum on Kerepesi Road”. This is where it will be cleaned and conserved in the coming weeks.

signals.title: Bultaco is BACK… kind of
signals.summary: Images taken at an off-road event in Spain have given us our first glimpse of the new Bultaco Rally GT 300, but the more you look, the more you realise that things may not be what they seem… The storied off-road brand Bultaco seems to be sparking back into life. After a few years of focusing on electric and pedal-assisted off-road bicycles and lightweight dirt bikes, we finally have our first glimpse of a new petrol-powered adventure model. Although the word ‘new’ in the sentence is doing a lot of heavy lifting here. Those of a certain, younger age might not be familiar with the brand, but Bultaco was once a very big player in the world of off-road, enduro, trials, short circuit and even road racing. The Easy Rider star, Peter Fonda, famously owned a 1968 Pursang 250 desert racer, and if you were looking for a lightweight and competition-focused machine in the 1950s and 60s, the Spanish brand was a name to consider. As with many famous names from the past, though, Bultaco’s history isn’t one with a happy ending. The Barcelona factory closed its doors in 1983, remaining this way until it was snapped up by the Pandora Future Group in 2014. What followed was the aforementioned range of electric bikes for all ages. 2026, it seems, is the year that the brand is looking to return to doing what it is most famous for – proper petrol-powered motorbikes. signals.title: Pemutihan Pajak Kendaraan 2026, Begini Cara Bayar Online Tanpa ke Samsat
signals.summary: Pemutihan Pajak Kendaraan 2026, Begini Cara Bayar Online Tanpa ke Samsat JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com - Masyarakat yang belum membayar pajak kendaraan bermotor kini bisa memanfaatkan program keringanan dari pemerintah daerah. Tak hanya menghapus denda keterlambatan, beberapa daerah juga memberikan kemudahan pembayaran secara online, termasuk di Jakarta. Melalui program ini, masyarakat yang memiliki tunggakan pajak kendaraan tidak perlu membayar sanksi administratif berupa bunga ataupun denda keterlambatan. Pemilik kendaraan cukup melunasi pokok pajak yang menjadi kewajibannya. Program pemutihan pajak kendaraan di Jakarta berlangsung hingga 31 Desember 2026. Penghapusan sanksi administrasi tersebut dilakukan secara otomatis melalui sistem informasi manajemen pajak daerah, sehingga wajib pajak tidak perlu mengajukan permohonan khusus untuk mendapatkan keringanan. Bagi masyarakat yang ingin memanfaatkan program ini, pembayaran pajak kendaraan bisa dilakukan secara langsung melalui Samsat terdekat ataupun secara online menggunakan aplikasi Signal.
